evidence: src/review.ts:541 binds harnessEnvironment to the executor's own array by REFERENCE (`const harnessEnvironment = executor.environment ?? []`, no copy). The two refusals read it at 542 and 546; executor.command() runs at 559; applyHarnessEnvironment iterates the same array object at 603. An entry appended inside command() is therefore copied into the child environment without having passed either refusal.

Executed end to end against dist/src/review.js with the real dispatchReview and a stub executor declaring only CODEX_API_KEY up front and pushing {name:GH_TOKEN} and {name:HOME} onto its own array inside command(): `dispatch ok: true`; `declaration after command(): ["CODEX_API_KEY","GH_TOKEN","HOME"]`; the launched child printed `{"GH_TOKEN":"gh-token-for-the-probe","HOME":"/tmp/p7c-rgjTYI/out/review-m6-p7-20260930t220157z-1c13c3/scrub-env/home","CODEX_API_KEY":"codex-key","creds":null}` while the kernel's real HOME was /tmp/p7c-rgjTYI/kernel-home.

So the bypass is real for the pre-existing refused-vocabulary check (GH_TOKEN reached the reviewer) and NOT real for this fix round's own property: HOME came back as the harness-owned scrub-env/home target and HOME/.git-credentials read null, because applyHarnessEnvironment re-applies the five redirections after the join regardless of what was appended. This fix round's subject is intact under the bypass; what the bypass defeats is refuseExtraAllowlist, which predates it.

Why low, agreeing with the orchestrator's ruling: the executor module is imported into the kernel's OWN process (src/review.ts:269) with the kernel's environment, and dispatchReview accepts its command() return as argv after only a non-empty-strings check (563). My probe's command() read process.env and chose argv freely, which is the same capability. A module willing to mutate its declaration after the check can pass any credential it can read in argv or write it to a file, so the refusal is not a boundary against a dishonest executor; it bounds an honest one's declaration, as DR-0065's grant bounds an honest reviewer. Recorded rather than dismissed because an HONEST executor that computes part of its declaration inside command() would also bypass the check silently, which is a correctness trap rather than a leak.
findings.concrete-fix: Copy the array where it is read, src/review.ts:541: `const harnessEnvironment = [...(executor.environment ?? [])];`. One line, no behaviour change for an honest up-front declaration, and it makes the checked list and the applied list the same list.
